description: Fresh post-Q6 external blind compatibility benchmark for KOMPOSOS with broader source diversity across battery, polymer, metal, ceramic, semiconductor, and glass pair families. Pair identities are separate from audit/blind_test_pairs.json, audit/ground_truth/*.json, prior audit/external_blind/*.json files, and audit/dev_compatibility/*.json.
selection_policy: Thirty-five source-backed pairs selected from external papers, reviews, handbooks, and public technical references. Labels are evidence-backed compatibility outcomes, not outputs from KOMPOSOS. This file must not be used for bridge tuning; misses should define a separate development set before any successor blind benchmark is reported.
holdout_policy: Freeze with SHA256 before first diagnostic run. Do not change scorer logic against this file. If results are inspected and used for development, treat this benchmark as spent for future blind claims and freeze a new benchmark.

schema.expected_compatible: true means the pair is reported as usable, stable, standard, or chemically acceptable under the cited context; false means reported incompatibility, decomposition, galvanic failure, immiscibility, or unsuitable direct interface.

pairs.citation: A review of current collectors for lithium-ion batteries, Journal of Power Sources 2021
pairs.evidence_basis: Aluminum foil is the standard positive-electrode current collector for layered oxide lithium-ion cathodes in passivating LiPF6 electrolyte systems.

pairs.citation: Jia et al., Current collectors for lithium metal anodes, Advanced Functional Materials 2020
pairs.manual_source: Jia et al., Current collectors for lithium metal anodes, Advanced Functional Materials 2020
pairs.evidence_basis: Copper foil remains a standard low-potential substrate and current collector for lithium-metal deposition and stripping studies.

pairs.citation: Mikolajczak et al., Lithium-Ion Batteries Hazard and Use Assessment, Springer 2011
pairs.evidence_basis: Nickel tab hardware is standard lithium-ion cell interconnect hardware and is compatible as a connector rather than as a collector foil.

pairs.citation: Zhang, Journal of Power Sources 2006, copper dissolution at high positive potentials in Li-ion batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: Copper is unsuitable for high-potential layered-oxide cathode collector service because it oxidizes and dissolves at positive-electrode potentials.

pairs.citation: A review of current collectors for lithium-ion batteries, Journal of Power Sources 2021
pairs.evidence_basis: Aluminum is not the standard low-potential collector for lithium-metal anodes and is not used as the default direct anode collector in conventional Li-ion practice.

pairs.citation: Scrosati and Vincent, Polymer electrolytes: the key to lithium polymer batteries, MRS Bulletin 2000
pairs.manual_source: Scrosati and Vincent, Polymer electrolytes: the key to lithium polymer batteries, MRS Bulletin 2000
pairs.evidence_basis: PAN-based polymer electrolyte systems have been studied with lithium cobalt oxide cathodes in rechargeable lithium polymer battery architectures.

pairs.citation: Polymer electrolytes for lithium batteries, Chemical Reviews 2004
pairs.manual_source: Polymer electrolytes for lithium batteries, Chemical Reviews 2004
pairs.evidence_basis: PAN-family gel and solid polymer electrolytes are compatible with moderate-voltage lithium-ion cathode systems including phosphate chemistry.

pairs.citation: Small things make big deal: powerful binders of lithium batteries and post-lithium batteries, Energy Storage Materials 2019
pairs.evidence_basis: PVDF remains a standard chemically robust electrode-binder family and is compatible with low-potential insertion-anode composites.

pairs.citation: Small things make big deal: powerful binders of lithium batteries and post-lithium batteries, Energy Storage Materials 2019
pairs.evidence_basis: Fibrillated fluoropolymer binder families, including PTFE, are used for mechanically resilient silicon-containing negative-electrode composites.

pairs.citation: Polymer electrolytes for lithium batteries, Chemical Reviews 2004
pairs.manual_source: Polymer electrolytes for lithium batteries, Chemical Reviews 2004
pairs.evidence_basis: Unprotected PEO electrolyte chemistry lacks the oxidative stability required for direct service against high-voltage layered-oxide cathodes such as NCA.

pairs.citation: PolymerDatabase.com, polymer blend compatibility and polarity mismatch notes
pairs.evidence_basis: Polyethylene and nylon 66 are immiscible without compatibilization because of strong polarity and hydrogen-bonding mismatch.

pairs.citation: Utracki, Polymer Blends Handbook, Springer
pairs.manual_source: Utracki, Polymer Blends Handbook, Springer
pairs.evidence_basis: ABS and EPDM belong to the family of impact-modified thermoplastic and thermoplastic-elastomer blend systems used for toughness enhancement.

pairs.citation: Coleman, Graf, and Painter, Specific Interactions and the Miscibility of Polymer Blends, Technomic
pairs.manual_source: Coleman, Graf, and Painter, Specific Interactions and the Miscibility of Polymer Blends, Technomic
pairs.evidence_basis: PAN and PMMA are a classic polar-polymer blend family with favorable dipolar interactions that support miscibility or near-miscibility behavior.

pairs.citation: PolymerDatabase.com, polymer blend compatibility and polarity mismatch notes
pairs.evidence_basis: Polystyrene and PET are not a standard miscible direct blend and phase separate without compatibilizer chemistry.

pairs.citation: Victrex PEEK chemical resistance guide
pairs.evidence_basis: PEEK is widely cited as chemically resistant to acetone exposure at ambient conditions and is commonly cleaned or handled in such solvent environments.

pairs.citation: ASM Handbook Volume 13C: Corrosion: Environments and Industries
pairs.manual_source: ASM Handbook Volume 13C: Corrosion: Environments and Industries
pairs.evidence_basis: Silver-aluminum direct contact in conductive moisture creates a strong galvanic couple and is not a preferred direct service combination.

pairs.citation: Harman, Wire Bonding in Microelectronics, 3rd ed.
pairs.manual_source: Harman, Wire Bonding in Microelectronics, 3rd ed.
pairs.evidence_basis: Gold-aluminum direct bonding suffers intermetallic reliability problems such as purple plague and is not a universally compatible direct interface.

pairs.citation: ASM Specialty Handbook: Titanium and Titanium Alloys
pairs.manual_source: ASM Specialty Handbook: Titanium and Titanium Alloys
pairs.evidence_basis: Commercially pure titanium and titanium-base structural alloys are same-base materials with compatible passivation behavior in ordinary service.

pairs.citation: ASM Handbook Volume 3: Alloy Phase Diagrams and electrical contact practice references
pairs.manual_source: ASM Handbook Volume 3: Alloy Phase Diagrams and electrical contact practice references
pairs.evidence_basis: Silver and nickel are a common electrical-contact and plating combination with acceptable service compatibility in dry ambient conditions.

pairs.citation: Connector and plating stack technical references for gold-over-nickel finishes
pairs.manual_source: Connector and plating stack technical references for gold-over-nickel finishes
pairs.evidence_basis: Gold-over-nickel contact metallurgy is standard practice for stable, low-resistance electrical connectors and contact surfaces.

pairs.citation: Kingery, Bowen, and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics
pairs.manual_source: Kingery, Bowen, and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics
pairs.evidence_basis: Aluminum nitride and magnesia have dissimilar chemistry and processing constraints and are not a straightforward direct co-fired ceramic pairing.

pairs.citation: Rahaman, Ceramic Processing and Sintering
pairs.manual_source: Rahaman, Ceramic Processing and Sintering
pairs.evidence_basis: Silicon carbide and tungsten-carbide families are both used in refractory hard-material composite and wear-system contexts.

pairs.citation: Kingery, Bowen, and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics
pairs.manual_source: Kingery, Bowen, and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics
pairs.evidence_basis: Nitride-oxide direct ceramic integration between AlN and TiO2 is chemically and thermally constrained without engineered interlayers.

pairs.citation: Rahaman, Ceramic Processing and Sintering
pairs.manual_source: Rahaman, Ceramic Processing and Sintering
pairs.evidence_basis: Boron-carbide and tungsten-carbide materials belong to the hard-ceramic and armor/wear composite family of refractory systems.

pairs.citation: Richerson, Modern Ceramic Engineering
pairs.manual_source: Richerson, Modern Ceramic Engineering
pairs.evidence_basis: Alumina and silicon nitride have distinct densification chemistry, bonding behavior, and thermal design constraints, so they are not a default direct package-integration pair.

pairs.citation: Stringfellow, Organometallic Vapor-Phase Epitaxy: Theory and Practice
pairs.manual_source: Stringfellow, Organometallic Vapor-Phase Epitaxy: Theory and Practice
pairs.evidence_basis: AlAs on Ge is a difficult heterovalent and mismatched semiconductor pairing rather than a default directly compatible epitaxial interface.

pairs.citation: Morkoc, Handbook of Nitride Semiconductors and Devices
pairs.manual_source: Morkoc, Handbook of Nitride Semiconductors and Devices
pairs.evidence_basis: GaN on Si requires heavy buffer and stress-management engineering because of severe thermal and lattice mismatch, so it is not a default direct interface.

pairs.citation: Nomura et al., room-temperature fabrication of transparent flexible thin-film transistors using amorphous oxide semiconductors, Nature 2004
pairs.evidence_basis: ZnO-family transparent conducting and oxide-semiconductor layers are part of the same oxide-electronics process space as IGZO thin-film stacks.

pairs.citation: Review articles on ultra-wide-bandgap oxide semiconductors and oxide electronics integration
pairs.manual_source: Review articles on ultra-wide-bandgap oxide semiconductors and oxide electronics integration
pairs.evidence_basis: Gallium-oxide and IGZO are both oxide semiconductor families and can be treated as compatible within heterogeneous oxide-electronics stack contexts.

pairs.citation: People and Bean, band alignments and strain-layer superlattices in Ge/Si systems, Applied Physics Letters 1985
pairs.manual_source: People and Bean, Si/Ge heteroepitaxy references, Applied Physics Letters 1985
pairs.evidence_basis: Si/Ge heteroepitaxy and SiGe technology are canonical semiconductor integration families under strain-managed growth conditions.

pairs.citation: Schott optical glass and fused silica thermal-expansion data references
pairs.manual_source: Schott optical glass and fused silica thermal-expansion data references
pairs.evidence_basis: BK7 crown glass and fused silica have strongly different thermal expansion behavior and are not a default direct fusion-seal pair.

pairs.citation: Schott Zerodur and fused silica optical-assembly references
pairs.manual_source: Schott Zerodur and fused silica optical-assembly references
pairs.evidence_basis: Low-expansion optical glasses and fused silica are compatible in precision optical assemblies when the process is adhesive, contacted, or mechanically mounted rather than fused.

pairs.citation: Varshneya, Fundamentals of Inorganic Glasses
pairs.manual_source: Varshneya, Fundamentals of Inorganic Glasses
pairs.evidence_basis: Borosilicate and soda-lime float glasses have different composition and expansion behavior and are not a default direct fusion-seal pairing.

pairs.citation: Varshneya, Fundamentals of Inorganic Glasses
pairs.manual_source: Varshneya, Fundamentals of Inorganic Glasses
pairs.evidence_basis: Bioactive silicate glass compositions and high-silica glass have incompatible direct thermal-processing windows for simple fusion-seal service.

pairs.citation: Schott low-expansion glass data and soda-lime float property references
pairs.manual_source: Schott low-expansion glass data and soda-lime float property references
pairs.evidence_basis: Zerodur-class low-expansion optical glass and soda-lime float glass are not a default direct precision optical interface because of major property mismatch.
